value.title: Change a live Copilot seat's model or effort
value.summary: Relaunch a running Copilot seat on a new `--model`, `--effort` or both in the same pane, resuming the same conversation, with its pij identity kept and its cache-proxy environment kept, rewritten or dropped as the model needs. Replaces docs/how/change-seat-effort.md.

value.who: The operator, or the prime or the seat's parent with the operator's yes. Never the seat itself: the relaunch ends its own process.
value.when: When the operator wants a live Copilot seat on a different model or effort without losing its context. Run it with `--key <seat>`.

value.name: model
value.description: the new model id, as Copilot's `--model` takes it (e.g. claude-opus-5.5, gpt-5.5); letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-' only, anything else is refused. Give a model, an effort or both
value.fallback: leave it out to keep the seat's model; for a new one, discover the exact id at runtime and canary it before use (pij skill, shared convention C4), because the script can't check it against Copilot's list

value.name: effort
value.description: the effort, one of none, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh or max (`copilot --help`, --reasoning-effort); anything else is refused. Which ones work depends on the model, and a HydraFusion model takes none
value.fallback: leave it out to keep the seat's effort; ask the operator which effort

value.title: Get the operator's yes
value.done_when: The operator agreed to relaunch this seat now.

value.title: Relaunch the seat in its pane on the new model or effort
value.done_when: The seat's process runs with exactly `--model <model>` and `--effort <effort>` (whichever were given), resumed on the same session, in the same pane, and with the cache-proxy environment its model needs: none for a model that is not Claude, the proxy's id for a Claude model on a proxied seat.

pre.fix: Wait until `pij list` shows the seat idle with an empty composer; only Copilot seats take this procedure.

value.proven_in_practice: Live on pij-capable-marten, 2026-11-26, by pij-solid-ox with both primes' yes (claude-opus-5.5, xhigh, through the cache proxy, same flags: a no-op run). Same pane and session, all five COPILOT_PROVIDER_* carried, liveness active, role and parent unchanged; the record stayed stale (l-1, l-2). Earlier by hand on the same seat, 2026-11-23 (medium to xhigh).
value.note: The cache-proxy rule is the daemon's spawn gate (crates/daemon/src/cache_proxy.rs; docs/how/cache-proxy.md): only a Claude model goes through the proxy. A model that is not Claude runs plain Copilot, so the relaunch drops every COPILOT_PROVIDER_* variable. A Claude model on a proxied seat keeps them, with COPILOT_PROVIDER_MODEL_ID set to the model's base id (a trailing -1m stripped) and COPILOT_PROVIDER_MAX_PROMPT_TOKENS to the limit `pij-rs cache-proxy status` lists for it; the step refuses, changing nothing, when the proxy is not ready or does not list that model. A new model also gets `--context long_context` (`default` for a HydraFusion model), as pij's spawn gives it (crates/harnesses/src/spawn.rs).

value.title: Check it re-registered with its context
value.done_when: `pij list` shows the seat on its new process with its extension build, its footer shows the new model or effort with the context figure unchanged, and `show` prints the cache-proxy environment the model needs.

sections.name: done_when
sections.value: The seat runs on the new model or effort, resumed with its context, with the cache-proxy environment its model needs, and pij lists it registered on the new process.

value.text: The relaunch does not refresh pij's record of the seat: `pij-rs list` keeps the model and effort pij launched it with (`pij sessions --history --seat <seat>` too), and a later `pij-rs revive` puts the seat back on them. `pij-rs revive <seat> --model <id>` revives on a new model; `pij revive --effort` is an open item in the operator's queue. Seen live on 2026-11-26: after a relaunch on xhigh the record still read medium.

pij records the relaunched seat's route as none (`cache_proxy: null` in `pij-rs list`), not proxied: the new process doesn't descend from the launch the daemon stamped (F213). A Claude seat's traffic still goes through the cache proxy, because the COPILOT_PROVIDER_* environment came with it (check the pane's process with `ps -Eww -p <pid>`).
The relaunched process runs without `pij-rs __spawn-child`, so if it exits there is no exit-status file or launch log for a post-mortem.
The seat's flags come from `ps`, which joins arguments with spaces, so a flag value that holds a space comes back as two words.

A PIJ_* or COPILOT_* variable whose name holds KEY, TOKEN, SECRET, PASS, CREDENTIAL or AUTH is not carried (req-13). The script names each one it leaves out; a seat that needs one must get it again another way.

A seat that ran plain stays plain on a new Claude model: only a pij spawn or revive runs the cache-proxy gate, and the script says so. To put it behind the proxy, revive it on that model (`pij-rs revive <seat> --model <id>`) once its process has ended.

The script checks a model id's shape, not that Copilot serves it. A model Copilot refuses ends the new process, and the pane with it; rerun the procedure with the old model (`pij sessions --history --seat <seat>` names it) or revive the seat.
Dropping the COPILOT_PROVIDER_* environment of a seat that stays on Claude: the seat silently leaves the cache proxy and its next wake after five minutes idle rebuilds its whole context.
Carrying PIJ_SPAWN_ID: it ties the new process to a spawn that has finished.
Leaving out --resume=<session>: the seat starts a new conversation and loses its context.

Using `/settings effortLevel` (changes the default for every new session), `/restart` (keeps the old flag) or `/model` in the session (the process keeps the launch's COPILOT_PROVIDER_* environment, which names the old model and, for a model that is not Claude, sends it to the Anthropic-only proxy).

Putting the seat's environment on the respawn command line: every value is then readable through `ps` by any local user and logged by the endpoint scanner. The script passes values through a 0600 file the pane reads and deletes.
Keeping COPILOT_PROVIDER_* when moving a seat to a GPT (or any other non-Claude) model: the proxy serves Claude models only, so the model must run plain Copilot.

Treating COPILOT_PROVIDER_MAX_PROMPT_TOKENS as a secret because its name holds TOKEN: it is the model's prompt limit, and dropping it leaves a proxied seat without its 1M window. The script carries it by exact name.

Reading the seat's flags and environment from pij's recorded pid. After a Copilot `/restart` that process is the loader's child: its argv has no --model or --effort, and its environment holds the loader's own variables. The script reads the pane's own process (`tmux display-message -p -t <pane> '#{pane_pid}'`), which is the launch.

value.why: The spawn gate whose rule s0002 repeats: only a Claude model is proxied, as its base id, with the limit the proxy lists. If the gate changes, change relaunch.sh with it.
How pij launches a Copilot seat: the COPILOT_PROVIDER_* names and the `--model`/`--context` flags s0002 sets the same way.
The cache proxy itself: what it serves, `pij-rs cache-proxy status`, and where to read a seat's route (`ps -Eww`, never an env check inside the seat).

value.change: Covers the model as well as the effort (the gap found 2026-11-24): a model input, the cache-proxy rule (a model that is not Claude runs plain Copilot and drops COPILOT_PROVIDER_*; a Claude model on a proxied seat keeps them with the proxy's id and limit), the done check renamed flags-are, and the folder renamed to match. Fixed: the secret filter dropped COPILOT_PROVIDER_MAX_PROMPT_TOKENS (its name holds TOKEN). Written with PROC-meta-0001, in the operator's approved scope of 2026-11-26 09:13.
Status draft → current; approved by operator (2026-11-26 09:13, "get procedures stuff in as well": approves PRD 005 and its procedures (prime packet procedures-current)); recorded by pij-solid-ox.

Live run (req-24) on pij-capable-marten found the script read pij's recorded pid, a Copilot restart child with no --model or --effort; it now reads the pane's own process, and skips launcher words up to the copilot entry point (m-8). l-1 and l-2 now say what the live run showed: the record stays stale.
